text:
You’re looking for a full stack collaborator to build a GPT playground clone that makes prompt testing faster, easier, and more extensible than the current OpenAI experience.

I’m Noor Halden, and I’d be excited to help you shape this into a practical tool you can keep improving week by week. I have 6 years of experience working with Python, PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, and machine learning, and I enjoy building AI products that are useful in day-to-day workflows rather than just impressive in demos.

A relevant project I’d point to is a Delivery support chatbot for Parcelwise Logistics. I built a WhatsApp and SMS assistant using Python, OpenAI API, LangGraph, FastAPI, Redis, and Twilio. It tracked parcels, rescheduled deliveries, and handed off to a human with full context when needed. The result was 43% of conversations resolved without an agent, with CSAT at 4.4 out of 5. That project required careful prompt handling, tool calling, orchestration, and designing a reliable user flow around an AI system — all of which map well to what you want here.

For your GPT playground clone, I’d be comfortable helping with both the AI-facing and product-facing parts: prompt input and parameter controls, model interaction patterns, structured response handling, and building a clean workflow for rapid iteration. Since you want this to become a long-term collaboration, I like the idea of starting with a solid clone and then layering in features that make experimentation faster and more enjoyable.

I also like that you called out “megaprompt” — that kind of energy around experimenting with prompts is exactly the sort of project I’d enjoy working on. If you want someone practical, collaborative, and comfortable turning AI ideas into usable tools, I’d be glad to talk.
